name: Los Yesares positions, Pinto
story: South of Madrid, between Pinto and Valdemoro, the Nationalist line that ran from the Cerro de los Ángeles to the Jarama was dug into the gypsum hills. At Los Yesares, archaeologists of the Comunidad de Madrid have recorded four concrete-and-masonry posts, trenches, rifle pits and a shelter on a limestone hill. The site shows the static rear lines that followed the Jarama battle. A similar Nationalist position was excavated at El Espartal near Valdemoro.
see: Four small fortins, trenches and a shelter on a low hill.
plan: Accessible on foot from Pinto; little signage, so use a GPS track. Free.
